title: Sattar&Co. advises on a significant cross-border acquisition in Bangladesh’s textile and apparel sector
excerpt:
Sattar&Co. is pleased to highlight its role in advising on a significant share acquisition in Bangladesh’s textile and apparel sector. Sattar&Co. acted as legal counsel in connection with the acquisition of foreign shares in a Bangladeshi textile mill by a renowned readymade garments company.
The transaction involved a number of cross-border legal and commercial considerations. Sattar&Co. was involved throughout the transaction, including conducting and advising on the legal due diligence process, reviewing the corporate and commercial documents of the target company, identifying and assessing potential legal risks, and assisting with drafting the relevant transaction documentation and completion process.
The successful completion of the transaction reflects the importance of thorough due diligence, effective transaction structuring, and close coordination among stakeholders in cross-border corporate transactions.

title: Sattar & Co. Advises Japanese Shareholder on Chairman Appointment Dispute
excerpt:
In a recent corporate advisory matter, Sattar&Co. is advising a Japanese shareholder in connection with a Boardroom dispute relating to the appointment of the Chairman of a limited company.
The appointment, ratified pursuant to passing a resolution at the Extraordinary General Meeting (EGM), was done in contravention of the shareholders' agreement and the expectation amongst the minority shareholders.
The matter raised an important corporate governance question: Can a shareholder disregard a contractual obligation contained in a shareholders' agreement when making a corporate decision affecting the rights and interests of another shareholder?
Sattar&Co. is advising the Japanese shareholder on the available legal remedies for challenging such a decision and safeguarding the affected shareholders' rights and interests.

title: Sattar&Co. advises international organization on disputed supplier invoices and procurement-related claims
excerpt:
Commercial deals often continue on the basis of long-standing relationships, informal purchase arrangements and operational urgency. However, when underlying documentation is incomplete and historic invoices remain unpaid, parties may face significant legal and evidentiary questions regarding payment obligations and contractual liability (especially when fraud is alleged).
Sattar&Co. is currently advising an international organization in Bangladesh on the legal implications of several outstanding supplier invoices relating to past procurement of goods and technical works, where the available records (including invoices, delivery receipts etc.) remain incomplete and where fraud is alleged. The exercise involves analysis of available evidence, investigations surrounding the allegations of fraud and legal remedies available to the client (including non-payment of the disputed invoices).
Our advice involves examining the relevant provisions of the Contract Act 1872, the Sale of Goods Act 1930 and the Evidence Act 1872 to assess the burden of proof in payment disputes, the evidentiary value of signed delivery receipts by unauthorized staff and the legal consequences of informal purchasing arrangements.
The matter highlights the importance of maintaining robust procurement records, clearly documenting contractual arrangements, delivery acknowledgements and pricing terms, while recognizing that consistent business dealings and implied contractual relationships may still create legally enforceable obligations under Bangladeshi law.

title: Sattar&Co. advises Japanese company on a major investment in Bangladesh’s ship recycling sector
excerpt:
Bangladesh has developed a significant position in the global ship recycling industry. The sector plays an important role in the country's economy and contributes to employment, steel production, recycling and related industrial activities.
Sattar&Co. is currently advising on the structuring of a major investment by a renowned Japanese company in a leading Bangladeshi ship breaking and recycling company.
Sattar&Co.'s current advice on this matter involves drafting the initial MoU, due diligence and then drafting/reviewing the key definitive agreements. Other key considerations relate to structuring the investments, including research of the applicable legal and regulatory requirements for foreign investments in such sector.
This transaction marks another notable example of Sattar&Co.'s dynamic Mergers and Acquisitions (M&A) practice.

title: Sattar&Co. advises global technology company on digital signature regulations in Bangladesh
excerpt:
Sattar&Co. is pleased to highlight its recent advisory to a leading global technology company on the legal and regulatory framework governing the use and implementation of digital signatures in Bangladesh.
As businesses increasingly embrace digital transactions, the use of electronic and digital signatures is becoming an important aspect of commercial, corporate and technology-driven operations in Bangladesh. However, the legal validity of such signatures does not depend solely on the electronic execution of a document. It requires compliance with the statutory and regulatory framework governing the authentication and certification of electronic transactions.
Sattar&Co. has recently advised a leading global technology company on the legal and regulatory framework applicable to the use and implementation of digital signatures in Bangladesh.
The advice involved examining the relevant Information and Communication Technology Act, the Information Technology (Certifying Authority) Rules (the "CA Rules"), the Bangladesh Root CA Certification Practice Statement and the regulatory guidelines issued by the Controller of Certifying Authorities (CCA). Particular consideration was given to the requirements relating to authentication, digital certificates, licensed Certifying Authorities and the use of secure electronic signatures. The advice also addressed data protection and cross-border data transfers, including the requirements under the Personal Data Protection Act, and the restrictions under the CA Rules concerning the transfer of confidential subscriber information and the location of relevant certificate-processing infrastructure.

title: Sattar&Co. successfully represents leading Bangladeshi company in shareholder dispute
excerpt:
Sattar&Co. recently successfully represented a leading Bangladeshi company and its majority shareholders in a shareholder dispute.
The case originated from an application filed by a minority shareholder of the Bangladeshi company under Section 233 of the Companies Act, 1994 raising various allegations relating to siphoning of company funds and mismanagement. The minority shareholder also sought the special audit of the company by appointing an independent auditor.
Following comprehensive submissions from both sides, the Hon'ble Companies Court was pleased to reject the minority shareholder's arguments and also the application seeking the appointment of an independent auditor in favour of Sattar&Co. The case involved important points of law surrounding minority shareholder protection rights, corporate governance, AGMs, and the extent of judicial intervention in the internal affairs of the Company.
The decision represents a significant outcome for many companies entangled in internal shareholders' disputes and underscores the importance of preserving the legitimate autonomy of companies in conducting and managing its affairs in accordance with the applicable laws and its constitutional documents.

title: Sattar&Co. advises foreign investor on major container terminal project in Bangladesh
excerpt:
As Bangladesh continues to expand its role in regional and international trade, efficient and professionally managed container terminals are becoming increasingly important for the movement of goods, the competitiveness of businesses and the resilience of national supply chains. Container terminals are far more than physical gateways for moving cargo. They are the critical nodes connecting ports, global shipping networks, trade, logistics and the wider economy.
Sattar&Co. is advising a leading foreign investor in Bangladesh, currently engaged in the operation and management of port services under a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) arrangement, in connection with its proposed participation in another major container terminal management project.
Our advice focuses not only on the tender requirements themselves, but also on whether participation in the proposed project could have any implications for its existing contractual, financing, tax and operational arrangements. Another area of our advice concerns the tax implications of the proposed participation considering various tax incentives, exemptions etc. Given the significant capital requirements associated with the development and operation of container terminals, existing financing arrangements with international lenders and related finance documents were also examined.

title: Sattar&Co. advises leading real estate developer on mediation and settlement
excerpt:
Mediation is not simply an alternative to litigation. It is an opportunity for parties to step away from adversarial positions, understand the underlying interests of each other, and explore solutions that may preserve both the commercial relationship and the value of the underlying transaction.
Sattar&Co. recently advised a leading real estate developer in relation to a potential dispute arising out of the handover of a real estate project.
Following completion of the project, the landowner raised concerns regarding the building, which resulted in a delay in taking over the premises.
As legal counsel for the developer, we assisted the client through the mediation and settlement process, carefully addressing the contractual issues, facilitating constructive dialogue between the parties, and working towards a commercially workable resolution. The matter was ultimately resolved avoiding the need for a costly arbitration.

title: Sattar&Co. advises international organization on employment cessation under Bangladesh labour law
excerpt:
The legality of any sort of cessation of employment often depends on procedural compliance as well as substantive grounds. Even where a valid reason exists, failure to follow the prescribed legal process may expose employers to unnecessary legal risks.
Recently, Sattar&Co. advised an international organization operating in Bangladesh on various employment law issues relating to the cessation of employment under the Bangladesh Labour Act, 2006.
The advice involved analyzing the available statutory mechanisms for cessation of employment, reviewing the procedural requirements applicable under Bangladeshi labour law, and advising on the legal implications of employee entitlements and recovery of employment-related payments.
